task.description: git checkout feature/WF03-ISS0720-20260919 first. Design the fix for ISS-0720's root cause: read result.summary of step-01-issue-fixer-diagnosis.json (artifacts_in) in full for the diagnosis and ISSUE-FIXER's recommendation. Design must specify, as interface/signature-level changes only (no implementation bodies, per this project's design-artefact rules): (1) oidc_issuer_base/0's replacement logic reading Application.get_env(:letflow, :oidc, [])[:keycloak_base_url] instead of the retired :issuer key -- note keycloak_base_url is already a bare base URL (no /realms/<slug> suffix, confirmed by config/runtime.exs's own derive_base_url_from_legacy_issuer comment and value shape), so the existing String.split("/realms/") stripping logic in the current oidc_issuer_base/0 must be removed, not merely re-pointed at a new key -- state this explicitly as a design element, do not leave it implicit. (2) A decision, with stated rationale, on whether @default_idp_base_url ("http://localhost:8082") stays as a fallback for every environment or is scoped to fail loudly (raise, or an explicit warning/error condition) outside Mix.env() in [:dev, :test] -- ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis recommends the latter; you are the design authority and may agree or diverge, but must state your reasoning either way, and if you scope it, specify exactly what happens instead in a non-dev/test environment with no real base URL resolvable (raise at call time vs. at boot vs. a logged error with the literal default retained as belt-and-suspenders -- pick one and justify it against this endpoint's own moduledoc's 'never error to the caller' rule, which governs the TENANT/DB-lookup response shape, not this config-resolution path -- do not silently let that rule block your decision without addressing it explicitly). (3) No new public function, module, or @spec beyond what's needed to express this -- if the fix is a small function body change, a design doc's job here is to state the target logic in words/pseudocode-free interface terms, not to prescribe unnecessary structure for a 1-2 function fix. Write the design artefact to lib/letflow/design/iss0720-tenant-config-stale-issuer-key.md, following this project's existing design-doc conventions (see other files in lib/letflow/design/ for shape/precedent).
acceptance_criteria: Explicitly states the :keycloak_base_url key rename and the removal of the /realms/ stripping logic

Explicitly decides and justifies the localhost-default fallback question (keep-always vs. dev/test-scoped-with-fail-loud-elsewhere), addressing the moduledoc's never-error rule directly rather than ignoring it
Contains no .ex implementation code bodies (interface/signature/pseudocode-free description only, per this project's CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR check (e))
Design is a fix to an existing private function -- no new public function/module/@spec is introduced unless genuinely required, and the doc states explicitly why or why not

result.summary: Design written to lib/letflow/design/iss0720-tenant-config-stale-issuer-key.md. (1) oidc_issuer_base/0: repoint Application.get_env(:letflow, :oidc, [])[:issuer] to [:keycloak_base_url], AND explicitly remove the String.split("/realms/")|>List.first() stripping -- keycloak_base_url is already a bare base URL (confirmed via config/dev.exs:88-90's REQ-370 comment and config/runtime.exs:141-146's derivation, which shows keycloak_base_url is upstream of any /realms/ suffix, not downstream); config_map/2 already appends "/realms/" <> realm_id itself, so the old stripping is dead-at-best, silently-truncating-at-worst against the new key's shape. (2) Traced (not assumed) what actually reaches @default_idp_base_url after the key fix: config/dev.exs and config/test.exs always set a real keycloak_base_url, and config/runtime.exs's own :prod block always sets one too (env var, legacy-derivation, or its own "https://placeholder-keycloak.invalid" literal) -- so tenant_config.ex's own localhost fallback becomes reachable only when the :letflow, :oidc app env is entirely unpopulated (a release/boot defect, not a missing env var). Despite that narrower exposure, agree with ISSUE-FIXER's recommendation: scope @default_idp_base_url to dev/test only, via a new compile-time module attribute @allow_localhost_idp_fallback? = Application.compile_env(:letflow, :allow_localhost_idp_fallback, false) -- mirrors this codebase's own established pattern (activation.ex's @activation_test_hooks_enabled?, explicitly rejecting a runtime Mix.env() check since Mix is unavailable in a compiled release) rather than inventing a new convention; config/dev.exs and config/test.exs each need one companion line (config :letflow, :allow_localhost_idp_fallback, true), prod/runtime.exs add nothing. Outside dev/test, idp_base_url/0 raises at call time instead of returning the literal, once no real value resolves from either env var or keycloak_base_url. Reckoned directly with the moduledoc's never-error/INV-5 rule (not sidestepped): that rule is scoped to the realm/tenant-resolution branch (resolve_realm/2 + DB lookup), whose failure varies per-request/per-tenant, where masking preserves availability for unaffected tenants and avoids a tenant-existence oracle; idp_base_url/0's failure is uniform across every request/tenant on a given boot -- no availability to preserve across, no tenant signal to leak -- so a loud, immediate, whole-node failure caught by a smoke test/health check before real traffic is judged better than the plausible-looking 200 that caused ISS-0719, at the accepted cost of a temporary 500 on this endpoint until redeploy. (3) No new public function/module/@spec: both changes are body-level edits to the two existing private functions plus one new private compile-time module attribute (same kind as activation.ex's precedent) -- explicitly justified in the doc's own S3. Open questions flagged rather than silently resolved: config/runtime.exs's own placeholder-keycloak.invalid fallback is a structurally identical problem one layer up but out of this fix's owned_modules scope (routed to REVIEWER to confirm the scoping call); and whether the raise branch is unit-testable given compile-time attributes don't respond to Application.put_env/3 at runtime is flagged for TEST-DESIGNER.
